headline: High-risk filesystem and network interaction: Claude Code can read/write shared files and egress broadly, while Airbyte can move business data over APIs.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Claude Code can read repo/user files and use MCP servers, so if Airbyte outputs are copied into shared files or MCP-fed prompts, malicious content could steer Claude Code. Airbyte itself is an API-based data tool with broad egress, but no direct parser bridge is documented. The pathway exists in shared-file workflows, not by default isolation.
conditions: IF Airbyte-generated content is written into a file that Claude Code reads as instructions
IF an MCP server forwards Airbyte output into Claude Code prompts without provenance checks
mitigations: Keep Airbyte outputs in data-only files, not prompt files
Disable MCP servers for sessions that ingest untrusted Airbyte output
Add a manual review step before Claude Code consumes Airbyte-generated text
Use separate directories for data artifacts and agent prompts

B_data_leakage.rationale: Airbyte touches business data and has broad network egress; Claude Code reads filesystem content and sends context to api.anthropic.com. If both share a workspace, Claude Code can ingest Airbyte-produced files and transmit them off-host. That creates a realistic leakage path for business data in default terminal workflows.
conditions: IF Airbyte writes business data into the shared cwd or repo files
IF Claude Code is run in the same workspace and includes those files in context
mitigations: Store sensitive Airbyte outputs outside Claude Code's workspace
Restrict Claude Code to a read-only sanitized subset of files
Redact business data before opening files in Claude Code
Use separate OS users or containers for the two agents
Turn off network access for Claude Code when handling sensitive exports

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Airbyte can call APIs and Claude Code can write the filesystem, modify git state, and spawn subprocesses. Their shared-state model is via filesystem and git only, so concurrent edits can collide on the same repo or artifacts. Because both have broad egress and mutable access, conflicts can corrupt work or overwrite changes in default multi-agent use.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same repository or output directory
IF Airbyte-generated artifacts are committed or rewritten while Claude Code is editing them
mitigations: Assign separate working directories
Serialize writes with a simple lock file
Require git pull/rebase before Claude Code commits
Have Airbyte write to immutable export paths
Pause one agent while the other performs file mutations

D_cascading_error.rationale: Claude Code can treat files as inputs and act on them with shell or git operations, so Airbyte-produced outputs may become authoritative without verification. Airbyte can generate data artifacts that Claude Code then uses to edit code or commit changes. The cascade is plausible in default workflows, but not inherently automatic because a human or workflow must connect them.
conditions: IF Claude Code is instructed to act on Airbyte-produced reports without validation
IF Airbyte outputs are used as source-of-truth inputs for shell or git actions
mitigations: Require a verification checklist before acting on Airbyte outputs
Separate generated data from decision inputs
Use diff review before any git commit by Claude Code
Mark Airbyte artifacts as untrusted in filenames or metadata

E_compliance.rationale: Airbyte touches business data and Claude Code handles files in the cwd plus git credentials in environment. If regulated or sensitive business data is placed in the shared workspace, Claude Code's cloud-backed context transmission can create retention and residency concerns. The profiles do not specify a concrete jurisdiction mismatch, so medium is the highest supportable severity.
conditions: IF regulated business data is stored in files accessible to Claude Code
IF organizational policy forbids sending those files to a third-party inference API
mitigations: Exclude regulated data from Claude Code workspaces
Use a local-only redaction step before analysis
Review retention and logging settings for Claude Code sessions
Keep secrets out of shared directories and environment variables
Consult a DPA or internal policy before processing regulated data
